source.title: Toward Moderate Overparameterization: Global Convergence Guarantees for Training Shallow Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves and numerically evaluates gradient-descent fitting of random labels in shallow one-hidden-layer networks, a conceptual test of training-error interpolation. Its results are theoretical and do not use the benchmark classification recipes in V1.
record.gate_note: The paper's own results include convergence guarantees for smooth and ReLU activations, SGD guarantees for smooth activations, a random-feature output-layer result, and numerical success probabilities for random regression labels. Excluded as rows: the output-layer result in Section 3, because it optimizes only output weights with random input weights, not the claimed gradient training from random initialization; cited CIFAR label-shuffling results are prior work. CIFAR and classification benchmarks are not evaluated.
record.test_reason: The study proves and numerically studies interpolation of real-valued regression labels by fully connected one-hidden-layer networks. It does not measure CIFAR training classification error in convolutional networks (V1), teacher–student spurious minima (V2), or any behavior specified by V3–V6. Its discussion of CIFAR label shuffling cites prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors establish geometric convergence guarantees for shallow networks trained over input-to-hidden weights with fixed balanced output weights, including smooth-activation SGD under a stated high-probability event. Their random-regression experiments suggest successful fitting near kd>n, a weaker overparameterization requirement than their theoretical guarantees. These conclusions concern regression interpolation rather than CIFAR classification.
record.recipe_differences: The work studies shallow scalar-output networks trained on quadratic loss, with fixed balanced output weights and random Gaussian input weights. It uses random regression labels and reports theory plus small numerical sweeps, rather than CIFAR classification recipes or deep benchmark models.
record.method_sensitivity: The required overparameterization differs by activation: the stated typical scaling is kd ≳ n² for smooth activations and kd ≳ n²/d for ReLU. Numerical success is swept over k and d and differs by activation and sample size.

fits_no_version.finding: Under specified data, initialization, fixed-output-weight, step-size, and overparameterization assumptions, gradient descent geometrically reduces shallow-network regression residuals to zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficiently overparameterized fully connected one-hidden-layer softplus and ReLU networks can interpolate arbitrary real-valued labels by gradient descent from Gaussian initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Random-regression experiments show a failure-to-success transition near kd=n as input dimension and hidden width increase; each configuration averages ten realizations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the tested shallow networks and random regression datasets, modest parameter overparameterization can suffice for gradient descent to achieve a small relative training residual.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Information Theory
record.problems: Numerical experiments use only 10 realizations per (k,d) pair and random regression data, not benchmark classification datasets. Figure 2's individual success probabilities are not tabulated. Theoretical results are restricted to shallow one-hidden-layer networks with particular fixed output weights and quadratic loss.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying result rows omitted. Section 3's random-feature least-squares result trains only the output layer while input-to-hidden weights remain random, so it does not measure the claimed gradient training from random initialization. Cited label-shuffling results are prior work, not this study's results.

untested.parts: Convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 using SGD or Adam, including random or corrupted labels and smaller-model, early-stopping, and regularization conditions.
Teacher–student spurious-local-minimum frequencies and the effect of one or two additional student neurons.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, and training very deep plain or normalization-free residual networks.
Comparisons of initialization schemes for signal propagation, training speed, or trainable depth.
Training above the initial stability limit, curvature adaptation, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The row states indicate that these measures cannot determine the supplied versions, not that regression interpolation failed. The study is not an original source for any supplied version. Its learning-rate and convergence-rate results do not test V4 or V5 because it neither compares initialization schemes nor examines stability-limit dynamics.

versions.untested_parts: Tests fitting random real-valued labels with shallow networks, including random-label numerical experiments, but not classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted benchmark labels, or comparisons involving smaller models, early stopping, and regularization.
The paper does not study teacher-student spurious minima or student width relative to teacher width.
The paper studies one-hidden-layer networks, not depth degradation or identity shortcuts.
Random Gaussian initialization is used, but initialization schemes are not compared for training speed or trainable depth.
No above-stability learning-rate regime or curvature dynamics are tested.
Batch normalization and normalization-free residual networks are not tested.

rows.subject: one-hidden layer neural network with softplus activation (Corollary 2.2)
rows.size_stated: k hidden units, d inputs; n training samples; kd ≥ Cn
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent on quadratic loss from i.i.d. N(0,1) input-to-hidden weights; hidden-to-output weights fixed with balanced signs.

conditions.value: i.i.d. uniform on unit sphere; labels not specified in Corollary 2.2

rows.measure: Training residual ∥f(Wτ)−y∥₂, with geometric convergence bound
rows.note: The convergence guarantee is for a real-valued quadratic-loss fitting objective; this is not a classification-error measure.
rows.check: Regression residuals in a fully connected shallow network do not measure V1. The width condition drops a square root: Corollary 2.2 requires sqrt(kd) ≥ Cn, hence kd ≥ C²n². The residual bound is 3(1−c1 d/n)^τ∥y∥₂, not 3(d/n)(1−c1)^τ∥y∥₂. Labels are arbitrary real values through the inherited theorem assumptions.

rows.subject: one-hidden layer neural network with ReLU activation (Corollary 2.4)
rows.size_stated: k hidden units, d inputs; n training samples; kd ≥ Cn²/d
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent on quadratic loss from i.i.d. N(0,1) input-to-hidden weights; hidden-to-output weights fixed with balanced signs.

conditions.value: i.i.d. uniform on unit sphere; labels not specified in Corollary 2.4

rows.measure: Training residual ∥f(Wτ)−y∥₂, with geometric convergence bound
rows.note: The convergence guarantee is for real-valued quadratic-loss fitting, not classification error.
rows.check: Regression residuals in a fully connected shallow network do not measure V1. Corollary 2.4 displays sqrt(kd) ≥ Cn²/d, hence kd ≥ C²n⁴/d². Its displayed step size is n/(∥y∥₂²∥X∥²), not ∥y∥₂²/(n∥X∥²). The residual bound is 3(1−c1 d/n)^τ∥y∥₂. Labels are arbitrary real values.
